title: How Two Brothers Stole 69,000 Bitcoin and Vanished
description:
In one of the biggest crypto heists in history, two South African brothers, Ameer and Raees Cajee, managed to steal over $4 billion in Bitcoin from their own investment platform, Africrypt. After claiming their company was hacked, they mysteriously vanished—along with the funds.

How did they pull off such a massive scam? Why did investors fall for it? And where are the brothers now?

Join us as we unravel the shocking story of the Africrypt scandal, exploring the tactics, deception, and unanswered questions behind this mind-blowing crypto heist.

🔔 Don’t forget to like, comment, and subscribe for more financial crime and  scams!

#BitcoinScam #Africrypt #CryptoHeist #TrueCrime #CryptoFraud

asr.full_text: April 2021, Johannesburg, South Africa. Clients of one of the continent's more promising crypto platforms, AfroCrypt, receive a disturbing message. The company announces a massive hacker attack. All investor funds, 69,000 Bitcoins worth $4 billion, have disappeared. The company's founders, brothers Amir and Raiyaz Khadji assure investors that an investigation is underway but urge them not to contact the police or lawyers, claiming it could harm the recovery process. At this very moment, the Khajiit brothers are already thousands of miles away, heading toward their destination. This is the story of how two young entrepreneurs pulled off one of the biggest scams in crypto history and vanished without a trace, taking four billion dollars with them. 2019. Johannesburg, South Africa. Amir and Raees Khaji. Young, ambitious, and confident. They believe they have found the perfect opportunity to make a fortune. The brothers create Africa Crypt, positioning it as a revolutionary platform that uses artificial intelligence for automated Bitcoin trading The promises sound fantastic. 10% profit per day. This means that investors can double their money in less than a month. The offer attracts wealthy investors. In South Africa, cryptocurrency is becoming a popular investment tool, and everyone wants to be part of the Crypto Revolution. Rapper nasty C promotes Afrikypt on social media, urging his followers not to miss the biggest investment opportunity of the decade. Footballer Benny McCarthy, one of South Africa's most famous players, also invests part of his earnings into the promising startup. Actress Charlize Theron, long interested in finance, decides to allocate part of her earnings for investment, even after the US goes through a process of revocations and negotiations. Even members of the ruling ANC party start taking an interest in the platform, seeing it as the future of the financial system. The Kaji brothers become stars. Their lives turn into an endless luxury spree, Lamborghini Aventador, Rolls Royce Ghost, Ferrari. Their car collection impresses even the wealthiest people in the country. They buy mansions, attend exclusive parties, and are featured in financial publications that call them the new leaders of the African financial market. But behind the glamorous facade lies a very different reality. In reality, a breakthrough financial platform is, in fact, a classic Ponzi scheme. Every day, hundreds of millions of dollars in Bitcoin pile up in AfriCrypt's accounts. To create the illusion of success, the brothers continue attracting more clients through aggressive marketing. They talk about plans to create Africa's first crypto bank and announce the launch of their own cryptocurrency africoin which they claim will outshine both bitcoin and ethereum but there is one problem if clients start withdrawing money in mass the system will collapse the kgs realize this and begin preparing for a grand exit first they need to discreetly transfer most of the assets to their own accounts. Next, they must find a country for a safe escape. The third step is creating a false narrative. Simply shutting down the platform will not be enough. They know that investors will demand their money back, and authorities will launch an investigation. So, they come up with the perfect way to avoid responsibility. They stage a hacker attack. Now, they just need to choose the perfect way to avoid responsibility, they stage a hacker attack. Now, they just need to choose the right moment to disappear. April 2021, AfriCrypt investors log into the platform as usual to check their balances. But this morning, something is off. Transactions are freezing and withdrawals are unavailable. At first, it seems like a technical glitch. But with every passing minute the situation becomes more suspicious. A few hours later, Afrikyp sends an official letter to its clients. It states that the company has suffered a massive hacker attack. All assets have disappeared. And any contact with the police or legal firms could jeopardize the recovery process. Instead of reassuring investors, the announcement only fuels their panic. The first thing defrauded investors do is try to contact customer support, but all phone numbers that used to answer instantly are now silent. The Afrocrypt website is gone. The company's building, which investors imagined as a high-tech financial center, turns out to be a small, ordinary house. No servers, no signs of an actual tech company. Those who understand blockchain begin analyzing transaction movements. It turns out that in the weeks leading up to the hacker attack, large sums started being withdrawn from AfriCrypt's main wallets. At first these were small transactions, but as the date of the scam approached, they became increasingly larger. crypto. The first was to trade that was sold to Crypto Inc. The second thing it did was to use crypto to scam cryptocurrency from other cryptocurrencies such as crypto. Crypto was made to be a commodity to use on Crypto. Other currencies, such as crypto, used crypto in the form of a cryptocurrency system, known as crypto currency. Crypto was then used more often by crypto and crypto currencies such as crypto, cryptocurrency and cryptocurrency. making it almost invisible. Then they were converted into stable coins, and later part of the funds was transferred to Monero. One of the most anonymous cryptocurrencies, which is nearly impossible to trace. The plan was simple. By the time Afro-Crypt officially announced the breach, most of the assets had already been moved beyond the reach of financial authorities. Investors try to contact the police, but when the investigation begins another shocking fact emerges. The Khaji Brothers never officially crossed South Africa's borders. According to passport control records, they were not among those who left the country. No airline tickets, no travel records, they vanished without a trace. This could mean only one thing, their escape was carefully planned in advance. Later, investigators discovered that a week before the hacker attack, employees at Afrikrypt, who had access to financial systems, one-by-one lost their login credentials. They could no longer log in, check balances, or make transactions. Access was revoked without warning and only the KG brothers had full control over the platform. The investigation expands internationally. Investors who lost their funds take action. Hanekom Attorneys files an official complaint with law enforcement, demanding an immediate investigation and the return of stolen funds. South African police launch a case, but quickly encounter a problem. There are no official records of the Kagji Brother is in the country anymore. News of the scam spreads worldwide. The case attracts not only local investigators, but also international organizations. Interpol officially places the brothers on its wanted list. Soon it becomes clear that the Kagji brothers had been preparing for their escape long before their disappearance. Several months before the scam, they and he's not saying they lost him. Soon it becomes clear that the Kaji brothers had been preparing for their escape long before their disappearance. Several months before the scam, they acquired citizenship in Vanuatu, a small island nation in the Pacific Ocean, that not only does not extradite its citizens or track financial transactions, but also provides visa-free access to 130 countries. Unofficial sources suggest they may have fled to Dubai, one of the world's largest financial hubs, where cryptocurrency is widely used in the shadow economy. Others point to Tanzania, a country where financial criminals have historically sought refuge. Some speculate they are in the United Kingdom under false identities. But none of these suspicions are officially confirmed. In 2023, Swiss investigators make a surprising And the first three years seem to be going very well for its business model for the new cryptocurrency chain that Asuric bought in the 1990s. But as a result, many customers are not interested in the crypto market. Asuric has a lot of information about a group of cryptocurrencies and people that were recently involved with them for their security and identity. But none of these suspicions are officially confirmed. In 2023, Swiss investigators make a surprising discovery. it cannot be accessed. Whether it belongs to the Keiji brothers or is just a coincidence remains unknown. Investors trying to recover their funds find themselves at a dead end. Despite the efforts of international investigators, no concrete evidence of the brothers' whereabouts exists. By 2024, the case reaches a dead end. The South African Financial Sector Conduct Authority makes an official statement. Since AfriCrypt was never registered as a financial Institution the government has no legal grounds for investigation this means only one thing no one will be held accountable so will the brothers ever be found or have the $4 billion permanently disappeared into the hands of scammers.
